newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Bonifacio says land demand still strong.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Bonifacio says land demand still strong.

text.p: Fort Bonifacio Development Corp, the developer of a 214-hectare lot at the edge of Manila's Makati financial district, dismissed fears the property sector is on the brink of collapse due to excess supply.
Bonifacio president Ricardo Pascua said Metro Pacific Corp's high-end residential condominium, the segment which was predicted to be the first to be hit, was still selling briskly.
"We have a healthy take-up in our Pacific Plaza," Pascua told stockholders.
He said 228 units out of the 390 units had already been reserved with cash down payment even though the building was yet to be built.
At present, there are nine residential and office buildings being built on the 15.9-hectare lot which has been sold to different developers.
"Our developers don't see any problem at the moment," he added.
Bonifacio is a joint venture firm between the Philippine government and a consortium of private sector developers led by Metro Pacific Corp.
Pascua also denied rumours that Filinvest Development Corp, one of the consortium's major members, is pulling out of the group. - MANILA NEWSROOM (63 2) 841-8938 Fax 817-6267
